deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a magnetometer damping (induction) experiment. A magnetic needle swings inside a multiplier (coil). The coil circuit is alternately open ('offen') and closed ('geschlossen'). When the circuit is closed, currents induced by the moving magnet damp the oscillation further. The previous page has swings 47-91 and ends with D.L. = 111.0 (open) and 638.4 (closed). The next page continues the series and gives a 'Recapitulation' of closed-minus-open decrements, averaging about 541.6.

Columns on this page:
- n: swing number.
- t: time of passage (h, ', ").
- A_n: amplitude (arc) in scale divisions.
- L_n = log10(A_n), to 5 decimals.

Open circuit:
- Swings 94-98: A = 574.05, 572.45, 571.05, 569.05, 567.55. L = 2.75895, 2.75774, 2.75668, 2.75515, 2.75400.
- Swings 110-114: A = 549.05, 548.1, 547.05, 545.6, 544.4. L = 2.73961, 2.73886, 2.73803, 2.73687, 2.73592.

Closed circuit:
- Swings 117-121: A = 526.75, 519.25, 511.55, 504.25, 496.85. L = 2.72161, 2.71538, 2.70889, 2.70265, 2.69623.
- Swings 133-137: A = 413.95, 407.9, 401.75, 395.4, 389.15. L = 2.61695, 2.61055, 2.60395, 2.59704, 2.59012.

Step 1 (group means). For each group of 5 consecutive swings, the mean log is taken. It is assigned to the middle swing:
- open: mean(94-98) = 2.75650 (at swing 96); mean(110-114) = 2.73786 (at swing 112).
- closed: mean(117-121) = 2.70895 (at swing 119); mean(133-137) = 2.60372 (at swing 135).
Averaging five swings suppresses reading errors in single amplitudes.

Step 2 (logarithmic decrement per swing, in units of 1e-5). For each pair of groups 16 swings apart, D.L. = (difference of mean logs)/16:
- open: (2.75650 - 2.73786)/16 = 0.01864/16 = 0.0011650, written as 116.50.
- closed: (2.70895 - 2.60372)/16 = 0.10523/16 = 0.0065769, written as 657.7.

Purpose: the closed-minus-open difference (657.7 - 116.5 ≈ 541.2) isolates the damping caused by the induced current. Air and internal damping are common to both states and cancel. Alternating the open and closed series compensates for slow changes during the run. On the next page this difference is tabulated for each successive pair and averaged (541.58).

Timing check (mine): the swing duration is about 42.35 s. For example, swing 98 (10h48'20.05") to swing 110 (56'48.2") spans 508.15 s over 12 swings, i.e. 42.35 s per swing. The duration is unchanged by closing the circuit.

Per-swing amplitude ratios implied (mine):
- closed: 10^-0.006577 ≈ 0.98497;
- open: 10^-0.001165 ≈ 0.99732.
errors: log10(571.05) = 2.756674, so to 5 decimals 2.75667; Gauss writes 2.75668 (last-digit slip of 1 unit, negligible).
log10(401.75) = 2.603956, so 2.60396; Gauss writes 2.60395 (last-digit slip of 1 unit, negligible).
All other logarithms, all four 5-term means and both decrements (116.50, 657.7) check correctly.

results.what: Determination of the logarithmic decrement of a swinging magnetometer needle from means of groups of amplitude logarithms, with the coil circuit alternately open and closed. The difference gives the electromagnetic (induction) damping.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement / measurement of eddy-current (induction) damping of a galvanometer magnet
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Wilhelm Weber, Göttingen magnetic work (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins, late 1830s); Weber's damping (Dämpfer) investigations

deep.surprise_reason: Routine reduction of observational data (logs, group means, decrements) in the Gauss–Weber damping/induction experiments, whose method is published and well known.
transcription_corrections: Swing 117 time is 11h 1' 44.5" (the '11' is the hour).
Swing numbers 133-136 appear overwritten in the image (e.g. 132→133, 133→134), but the final readings 133-137 match the transcription.
